niche_match.note: An ad is on-niche if `include` matches after `exclude` phrases are stripped. Pet insurance, dental-only, vision-only, Medicare Advantage and life insurance are adjacent verticals that share vocabulary — they are stripped before the include test so they do not pollute ACA angle and hook analysis. Medicare copy is SMID-gated on your side anyway and is a separate niche. Spanish-language ACA copy (seguro de salud, plan de salud, cobertura médica, subsidio) counts as on-niche — 115 of the baseline's raw ads were Spanish. Tightened 2026-09-12 after the baseline: 'licensed agent', 'ppo/hmo', 'copay', 'deductible' alone are call/insurance vocabulary, not ACA signals (they let Medicare Advantage call ads and an auto-glass shop through). Every 'Medicare' / 'Medi-Cal' / 'Medigap' mention is stripped before the include test; ACA ads that say 'not on Medicaid or Medicare' still match on their own terms. 'open/special enrollment' and '$0/month' alone were dropped from include (childcare enrollment ads and Medicare $0-premium D-SNP ads matched on them); ACA ads carry 'health insurance/plan/coverage', 'ACA', 'Obamacare', 'marketplace' or 'subsidy' anyway.

call_signals.note: Pay-per-call is the point of this niche. Every ad is additionally tagged as call-driven when ANY of these fire: cta_type CALL_NOW, CTA text 'Call now', a phone number in copy/title, or call language in copy. Reported as its own cut in REPORT.md. anti_regex marks ads that explicitly promise NO phone call (form / self-enroll funnels positioning against pay-per-call spam) — they are reported as `anti_call`, never as call-driven, unless they also carry a CALL_NOW CTA or a written phone number. tel: links are read from `url` AND from `xlinks` (extra_links).
